answer: A concrete defense is vouching with shared liability: a new agent enters only when an established agent stakes reputation on it, and if the newcomer cheats, the voucher loses part of its own stake. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging a whole trusted network is expensive, because each fake needs a real sponsor willing to risk loss. Around this kernel of accountability, suspicious behavior leaves an umber stain on the sponsor's record and a visible plume of linked failures, so sybil clusters are detected and cut off together rather than one by one.
